invariantsAffected: Multi-provider quorum review resilience without unhandled crashes
Deterministic finding addressing across verification lifecycle
records.technicalAnalysis: In src/core/harness.mjs:237-239, normalizeFinding directly preserves provider-local finding IDs: `id: raw.id !== undefined && raw.id !== null && String(raw.id).trim().length > 0 ? String(raw.id).trim() : ...`. When two distinct sentries (e.g. Sentry A and Sentry B) each report their first finding using the common local identifier 'finding-1' on different source files, aggregateConsensus (src/core/loop.mjs:471-500) does not merge them because their files/locators do not match. Consequently, both findings enter consensus with identical `id: 'finding-1'`. When this consensus is subsequently passed to conductIndependentVerification, src/core/independent-verifier.mjs:2014 immediately throws an unhandled exception: `Error: Producer findings contain duplicate finding ID 'finding-1' (DUPLICATE_FINDING_ID)`. In scripts/dogfood-review.mjs, this unhandled exception crashes the review run. Furthermore, src/core/harness.mjs:718-724 fails closed with `DUPLICATE_FINDING_ID`. Because neither normalizeFinding nor aggregateConsensus namespaces incoming finding IDs with their provider/source identity, valid multi-sentry reviews are prematurely aborted.
records.remediationSketch: In normalizeFinding or aggregateConsensus, namespace incoming provider-local finding IDs using the sentry provider/source role (e.g. `${source}:${raw.id}`) or assign deterministic consensus-scoped sequential IDs `finding-${i+1}` while preserving `providerFindingId` as audit metadata.
records.negativeTestContract: Given two sentry reports from distinct providers where sentry A emits finding-1 on fileA.js and sentry B emits finding-1 on fileB.js, when aggregateConsensus and conductIndependentVerification are executed, conductIndependentVerification MUST NOT throw DUPLICATE_FINDING_ID and both findings MUST be distinctly evaluable.

resolutionDetails.resolutionSummary: Remediated in Phase 1: in `normalizeFinding`, provider-local finding IDs matching generic numeric patterns are automatically namespaced (`${prefix}:${id}`) while preserving semantic IDs. In `_evaluatePostVerificationGateCore`, multi-pass finding resolution (`findEvaluationIndexForFinding`) and semantic content signature matching resolve evaluations without ID collisions.

invariantsAffected: Mandatory RunContext binding for verificationRecord gate authority
Fail-closed gating against ungrounded verification capabilities
records.technicalAnalysis: In src/core/harness.mjs:347 (_evaluateGateDecisionCore) and 593 (_evaluatePostVerificationGateCore), verification binding integrity checks (contentDigest, patchObjective, headSha, runId, exclusions) are executed strictly within `if (options?.runContext) { ... }`. When a caller provides a valid in-process verificationRecord (e.g. retained from a previous run on another changeset) but omits `options.runContext`, all binding integrity checks are silently bypassed. For a zero-finding consensus (`findings.length === 0`), the gate checks only `verificationRecord.verificationMode === 'clean_challenge'`, and then proceeds directly to approve at line 1147. A valid Clean Challenge record minted for ChangeSet A can therefore authorize an unrelated zero-finding review for ChangeSet B when runContext is omitted.
records.remediationSketch: Require mandatory presence of options.runContext whenever options.verificationRecord is supplied. In both _evaluateGateDecisionCore and _evaluatePostVerificationGateCore, if options.verificationRecord is present but options?.runContext is missing, fail closed immediately: `return { decision: 'block', reason: 'Gate Fail-Closed: Mandatory RunContext missing for verification record authority (MISSING_RUN_CONTEXT).', criticals: [], advisoryFindings: [] };`.
records.negativeTestContract: Given a zero-finding trusted consensus and a valid, trusted Clean Challenge verificationRecord, calling evaluateGateDecision(consensus, { verificationRecord }) without options.runContext MUST fail closed with decision: 'block' citing MISSING_RUN_CONTEXT and MUST NOT return 'approve'.

resolutionDetails.resolutionSummary: Remediated in Phase 1: in `_evaluateGateDecisionCore` and `_evaluatePostVerificationGateCore`, when `verificationRecord` is supplied and synthetic execution is not enabled, `options.runContext` is strictly mandatory. If missing or null, gate fails closed with reason 'Gate Fail-Closed: Mandatory RunContext missing for verification record authority (UNTRUSTED_OR_MISSING_RUN_CONTEXT).'

invariantsAffected: Robustness against malformed or hostile caller options
records.technicalAnalysis: In src/core/harness.mjs:348-350 and 594-596, plain object run contexts are converted via `new RunContext(options.runContext)`. The RunContext constructor in src/core/independent-verifier.mjs:231-233 throws an unhandled Error when runId contains path traversal sequences: `if (rawRunId.includes('..') || rawRunId.includes('/') || rawRunId.includes('\\') || rawRunId.includes('\0')) { throw new Error(...); }`. Because harness.mjs lacks a try/catch block around this constructor call, supplying options.runContext = { runId: '../escape' } crashes evaluateGateDecision and evaluatePostVerificationGate with an uncaught runtime exception instead of producing a structured, deterministic `{ decision: 'block' }` result.
records.remediationSketch: Wrap `new RunContext(options.runContext)` in a try/catch block in both _evaluateGateDecisionCore and _evaluatePostVerificationGateCore. Upon catching an Error, fail closed cleanly: `return { decision: 'block', reason: 'Gate Fail-Closed: Malformed RunContext (MALFORMED_RUN_CONTEXT): ' + err.message, criticals: [], advisoryFindings: [] };`.
records.negativeTestContract: Given a valid consensus, trusted verification record, and options.runContext = { runId: '../traversal' }, evaluateGateDecision and evaluatePostVerificationGate MUST NOT throw an unhandled exception and MUST return { decision: 'block' }.

resolutionDetails.resolutionSummary: Remediated in Phase 1: in `_evaluateGateDecisionCore` and `_evaluatePostVerificationGateCore`, instantiation of `RunContext` from caller options is enclosed in defensive `try/catch` blocks. Any constructor throw (such as path traversal in runId) returns deterministic fail-closed `{ decision: 'block', reason: 'Gate Fail-Closed: Malformed RunContext conversion failed (MALFORMED_RUN_CONTEXT_CONVERSION_FAILED): ...' }` instead of uncaught exception.

invariantsAffected: Mandatory strict binding validation on contentDigest and headSha
Fail-closed handling for malformed input fields
Defense against stripped digest/sha validation bypass
records.technicalAnalysis: In src/core/independent-verifier.mjs:186-222, normalizeDigest and normalizeCommitSha return empty strings `""` when passed non-empty strings that fail format validation (e.g. `normalizeDigest('invalid-sha') === ''`). When RunContext is constructed with a malformed digest or head SHA, its properties become `contentDigest = ''` and `headSha = ''`. In src/core/harness.mjs:354, 379, 600, and 625, the gate checks `if (rc.contentDigest) { ... }` and `if (rc.headSha) { ... }`. Because both properties were normalized to empty strings, the conditions evaluate to false and the binding checks are skipped entirely. A caller providing a malformed contentDigest or headSha effectively disables that axis of integrity validation rather than causing a fail-closed rejection.
records.remediationSketch: Require mandatory axes in RunContext to be non-empty and valid. In harness.mjs binding validation: `if (!rc.contentDigest || !rc.headSha) { return { decision: 'block', reason: 'Gate Fail-Closed: Malformed RunContext (MALFORMED_RUN_CONTEXT): contentDigest and headSha must be non-empty valid hex strings.', criticals: [], advisoryFindings: [] }; }`. Furthermore, validate in RunContext constructor that non-empty raw inputs that fail normalization throw or flag an invalid state.
records.negativeTestContract: Given a trusted zero-finding consensus and trusted Clean Challenge record, calling evaluateGateDecision with options.runContext = { contentDigest: 'invalid_non_hex', headSha: 'invalid_sha' } MUST fail closed with { decision: 'block' } and MUST NOT skip binding checks.

resolutionDetails.resolutionSummary: Remediated in Phase 1: in `_evaluateGateDecisionCore` and `_evaluatePostVerificationGateCore`, raw headSha and contentDigest values on `options.runContext` are validated against strict 40/64-char hex normalization. Non-empty invalid hex inputs fail closed with reason containing `MALFORMED_RUN_CONTEXT_BINDING` rather than bypassing verification.

invariantsAffected: Path exclusion scope integrity on case-sensitive filesystems
Scope binding immutability for verification records
records.technicalAnalysis: In src/core/harness.mjs:418-420 and 664-666, exclusions are compared after unconditional lowercasing: `const normRcExcl = rcExcl.map(s => String(s).trim().toLowerCase()).sort(); const normVrExcl = vrExcl.map(s => String(s).trim().toLowerCase()).sort();`. On POSIX/Linux systems, `src/Auth.js` and `src/auth.js` identify completely different physical files. Because exclusions are not bound into changeSet.diffHunks or digestChangeSet, this lowercasing enables a verification record minted with `src/Auth.js` excluded to be accepted for a RunContext excluding `src/auth.js`. This allows a verification performed under one scope to authorize a materially different scope on case-sensitive platforms.
records.remediationSketch: Preserve case during path exclusion comparison, or apply platform-aware normalization: normalize slashes to `/` across all platforms, and lowercase ONLY on Windows (`process.platform === 'win32'`). On POSIX platforms, retain exact case so distinct paths never compare equal.
records.negativeTestContract: On a case-sensitive platform (or in a platform-neutral unit test preserving case), given rc.exclusions = ['src/auth.js'] and vr.exclusions = ['src/Auth.js'], evaluateGateDecision MUST return { decision: 'block' } citing FORGED_OR_STALE_RECORD.

resolutionDetails.resolutionSummary: Remediated in Phase 1 (including P1-HARNESS-EXCLUSION-PLATFORM-OVERRIDE-01): implemented and exported `normalizeExclusionPath(s, { platform = process.platform })`. On POSIX platforms (`darwin`, `linux`), exact character casing is preserved while normalizing slashes and stripping `./`. On Windows (`win32`), casing is lowercased for filesystem comparison. Formal gate entry points strictly bind targetPlatform to host `process.platform`, ignoring caller `options.platform` override attempts; only isolated synthetic test gates (`allowSynthetic: true`) permit platform simulation.

invariantsAffected: Tamper-resistant finding set verification in post-verification gate
records.technicalAnalysis: In src/core/harness.mjs:559, getFindingSignature encodes finding fields into a single string by joining them with unescaped pipe characters: `${id}|${ruleId}|${title}|${file}|${lineStart}|${lineEnd}|${severity}|${cwe}|${type}|${recommendation}`. Because fields such as `title`, `file`, and `recommendation` can legally contain `|` (for example, in POSIX, `|` is a valid character in file paths), different findings can yield identical signatures. For example, Finding A with title 'foo|bar' and file 'baz' produces `||foo|bar|baz|1|1||||`, which is bit-for-bit identical to Finding B with title 'foo' and file 'bar|baz'. When bound findings are compared at line 793, delimiter collisions allow verifier evaluations to match materially different findings.
records.remediationSketch: Serialize the finding signature as a canonical JSON string (e.g. `JSON.stringify([id, ruleId, title, file, lineStart, lineEnd, severity, cwe, type, recommendation])`) or escape all pipe characters (e.g. `str.replace(/\|/g, '\\|')`) before concatenation to guarantee strict injectivity.
records.negativeTestContract: Given Finding A = { title: 'foo|bar', file: 'baz', line_start: 1, line_end: 1, severity: 'low' } and Finding B = { title: 'foo', file: 'bar|baz', line_start: 1, line_end: 1, severity: 'low' }, getFindingSignature(Finding A) !== getFindingSignature(Finding B).

resolutionDetails.resolutionSummary: Remediated in Phase 1: in `src/core/harness.mjs`, `getFindingSignature` serializes finding fields as a canonical JSON array tuple `JSON.stringify([id, ruleId, title, file, lineStart, lineEnd, severity, cwe, type, recommendation])`, providing collision-free, injective finding signatures.

invariantsAffected: Quorum and coverage validation before gate release
Consistent security posture across all exported gate entry points
records.technicalAnalysis: The exported function evaluatePostVerificationGate(consensus, verificationRecord, options) delegates to _evaluatePostVerificationGateCore. In _evaluatePostVerificationGateCore (lines 562-676), verificationRecord capability is validated, but consensus capability is NEVER validated. Line 677 unconditionally defaults findings: `const findings = Array.isArray(consensus?.findings) ? consensus.findings : [];`. If an external caller invokes evaluatePostVerificationGate with `consensus = null` (or an arbitrary plain object lacking trusted consensus) alongside a valid Clean Challenge record and matching RunContext, the function bypasses quorumReached, verdict, coverageOk, and capability checks, reaching line 1147 and returning `{ decision: 'approve' }`.
records.remediationSketch: Add the authoritative consensus capability and quorum checks from _evaluateGateDecisionCore to the beginning of _evaluatePostVerificationGateCore: verify `if (!isTrustedConsensus(consensus))` -> block UNTRUSTED_CONSENSUS; verify `if (!consensus.quorumReached || consensus.verdict === 'error')` -> block; verify `if (options?.coverageOk === false || consensus?.coverageOk === false)` -> block.
records.negativeTestContract: Calling evaluatePostVerificationGate(null, trustedRecord, { runContext }) or evaluatePostVerificationGate({ findings: [] }, trustedRecord, { runContext }) MUST return { decision: 'block' } with UNTRUSTED_CONSENSUS and MUST NOT return 'approve'.

resolutionDetails.resolutionSummary: Remediated in Phase 1: in `_evaluatePostVerificationGateCore`, consensus capability validation (`isTrustedConsensus(consensus)`) and quorum integrity checks (`!consensus.quorumReached || consensus.verdict === 'error'`) are executed prior to secondary checks. Null, undefined, or untrusted consensus immediately fails closed with `UNTRUSTED_OR_MISSING_CONSENSUS`.

It does NOT check `if (verificationRecord.verificationMode !== 'producer_verification')`. invariantsAffected: R1 / 007-C Strict RunContext Binding & Content Digest Invariance
Diff Hashing Injectivity & Terminal Whitespace Preservation
records.technicalAnalysis: In src/adapters/review-orchestrator.mjs lines 64-74, buildCanonicalRunContext computes sha256 digests over changeSet.diffHunks.trim() and normalizedDiff.trim(), and inserts both into computedDigests: 'const trimmedDiffDigest = normalizeDigest(crypto.createHash("sha256").update(changeSet.diffHunks.trim(), "utf8").digest("hex")); if (trimmedDiffDigest) computedDigests.add(trimmedDiffDigest);' (lines 70-73). In lines 94-107, computedDigests are collected into verifiedDigestCandidates. At line 118, if options.verificationRecord is provided, vrDigest is checked against verifiedDigestCandidates. If an authentic verification record was minted for a prior diff without trailing whitespace (e.g., '+value\n'), and subsequent code introduces trailing whitespace (e.g., '+value \n'), trimmedDiffDigest matches the old raw digest. Line 118 accepts the match, and line 123 sets selectedDigest = vrDigest. This allows stale verification records to bind to materially different diffs. Because terminal whitespace alterations can introduce behavioral changes or vulnerabilities in whitespace-sensitive formats (e.g., Python backslash continuations, Makefiles, string literals), diff hashing must be injective and only permit source-byte preserving normalizations like CRLF to LF.
records.remediationSketch: Remove trimmedDiffDigest and trimmedNormDiffDigest computations from buildCanonicalRunContext. (Target: src/adapters/review-orchestrator.mjs:70-73). Delete lines 70-73. Retain only rawDiffDigest and normDiffDigest (CRLF -> LF normalized). Ensure verifiedDigestCandidates only contains exact source bytes or line-ending normalized diff digests.

Create changeSetB with diffHunks ending in '+token  \n' (trailing spaces). Call orchestrateReview with changeSetB and recA. Expected: buildCanonicalRunContext returns null. orchestrateReview fails closed with gate.decision: 'block' and reason containing 'FORGED_OR_STALE_RECORD'.

invariantsAffected: R1 Strict RunContext Binding & Objective Immutability
records.technicalAnalysis: In src/adapters/review-orchestrator.mjs lines 174-186, buildCanonicalRunContext resolves patchObjective via precedence: 'const patchObjective = normalizeObjective(options.patchObjective || options.objectiveContract?.objective || options.runContext?.patchObjective || changeSet.patchObjective || changeSet.objectiveContract?.objective || "");'. When caller supplies an authoritative options.runContext, options.patchObjective silently overrides options.runContext.patchObjective without validating equality. An attacker or faulty caller can supply a legitimate RunContext for a security patch along with an overriding benign patchObjective and an unverified or mismatched record minted for the benign objective, and the canonical RunContext generated at line 198 will adopt the overriding objective rather than failing closed on the conflict. Conflicting objectives between options.patchObjective, options.objectiveContract, and options.runContext must be rejected.
records.remediationSketch: Add conflict detection for patchObjective and objectiveContract against options.runContext. (Target: src/adapters/review-orchestrator.mjs:173-186). If options.runContext?.patchObjective is defined, verify that normalizeObjective(options.patchObjective) matches normalizeObjective(options.runContext.patchObjective) if options.patchObjective is present. If there is a mismatch, return null (fail closed). Apply the same check for options.objectiveContract?.objective and changeSet.patchObjective.

Expected: buildCanonicalRunContext returns null, causing runContextMismatched = true and orchestrateReview to return gate.decision: 'block' with reason 'Gate Fail-Closed: Verification record binding mismatch (FORGED_OR_STALE_RECORD).'

invariantsAffected: R1 / 007-C Binding Execution Invariants & Replay Prevention
records.technicalAnalysis: Duplicate of PRRT_kwDOUWarIc6rr-JF. In src/adapters/review-orchestrator.mjs line 199, buildCanonicalRunContext resolves runId as: 'runId: options.runId || options.runContext?.runId || options.verificationRecord?.runId || null'. Although orchestrateReview generates a fresh runId at line 209 ('const runId = options.runId || crypto.randomUUID();') and passes it as the 3rd argument to buildCanonicalRunContext at lines 348 and 425 ('buildCanonicalRunContext(changeSet, options, runId)'), line 199 ignores the parameter 'runId'. records.technicalAnalysis: In src/adapters/review-orchestrator.mjs line 51, buildCanonicalRunContext is declared as 'function buildCanonicalRunContext(changeSet, options, runId)'. In orchestrateReview line 209, 'const runId = options.runId || crypto.randomUUID();' creates an authoritative run identifier. In lines 348 and 425, buildCanonicalRunContext(changeSet, options, runId) is invoked. However, in lines 198-205: 'return new RunContext({ runId: options.runId || options.runContext?.runId || options.verificationRecord?.runId || null, ... })'. The parameter 'runId' passed into the function is completely ignored. Instead, line 199 falls back to options.verificationRecord?.runId. Stale verification records can thus be replayed across runs.

If options.runContext?.runId and options.runContext.runId !== authoritativeRunId, return null. If vr?.runId and vr.runId !== authoritativeRunId, return null. In new RunContext({ runId: authoritativeRunId, ... }).

records.technicalAnalysis: In src/adapters/review-orchestrator.mjs lines 238-243: 'const isTier1Opt = options.tier === 1 || options.isTier1 === true; const diffTier = isTier1Opt ? 1 : (options.tier !== undefined ? If a caller passes options.tier = null, 'options.tier !== undefined' is true, and Number(null) evaluates to 0. If a caller passes an invalid string (e.g., 'invalid'), Number('invalid') evaluates to NaN. In both cases, computedHighestRisk (which correctly identified a Tier 1 sensitive diff, e.g. authentication or crypto files) is discarded. Downstream at lines 256, 301, 358, and 435, 'tier: diffTier, isTier1: diffTier === 1' sets isTier1 to false and tier to 0/NaN. In src/core/harness.mjs, evaluateGateDecision checks 'const isTier1 = options?.isTier1 === true || options?.tier === 1;', which evaluates to false. Consequently, Tier 1 changes are erroneously governed by Tier 2 policy: supported low omissions are approved as advisory rather than requiring human review, and supported medium omissions require human review rather than being blocked. Passing tier: null completely bypasses Tier 1 gate enforcement.

If options.tier is null or an unrecognized value, treat it as an error (fail closed) or ignore the override and fall back to computedHighestRisk.
